name: @payswap/onchain-security
description: Signer authorization + onchain security kernel (Work Order P4-W2, migration MMI-18/MMP-21+MMP-22): the deterministic security plane between intent preparation and user-controlled signing — provider-neutral identity contracts, exact-minor-unit write preparation, simulation OBSERVATIONS (never authority, INV-11), user-readable expected-state diffs, deterministic BLOCK/ALLOW/UNKNOWN gates over chain/asset/amount/destination/spender/expiry/route/protocol-identity/security-state/simulation-consistency, the trusted-approval-surface minting path for signed onchain authorization artifacts (INV-5), attenuated/revocable/expiring scoped signing delegation (INV-12), the immediate pre-broadcast recheck with stale-state invalidation (drift VOIDS, never auto-repairs), the consequential-write pipeline PREPARED→SIMULATED→GATED→DIFF_READY→AUTHORIZED→RECHECKED→BROADCAST_HANDOFF with terminal BLOCKED/VOIDED (INV-18/INV-3), signer adapters (EIP-712/ERC-1271 isolated behind ./adapters/* — never in core contracts, INV-17), the secret-boundary kernel (shapes+policy, redaction and opaque vault refs — NEVER key custody, INV-19/NON-CUSTODY), the encoded cannot_downgrade_block layer law (MODULE-OWNERSHIP security layer: a security gate can BLOCK, never un-block — INV-21, type + runtime), PLUS the onchain threat-intelligence vocabulary the security layer owns: the 13 threat families, evidence-chain-mandatory signals with integer-bps calibrated confidence, the versioned deterministic threat policy (ALLOW | ALLOW_WITH_CONSTRAINTS | REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION | BLOCK — authoritative), the adversarial analysis agent (deterministic, advisory only) and the no-downgrade verdict composition seam (an agent can only harden, never soften). Zero runtime dependencies; devDependencies are exactly the toolchain (typescript + vitest). ZERO sibling imports: no @payswap/* anywhere; contract shapes needed from the trust/capability lanes (AmountSpec, Principal, Mandate, ApprovalScope, SmartContractExtension, execution-quote disclosures, the declared state machine) are pinned STRUCTURALLY in src/pins/ — the accepted structural-mirror pattern; the Tech Lead wires the real lanes at integration.
